content: A neural network is a computing system inspired by biological neurons. It consists of layers of nodes that process inputs and learn patterns through training.
Training is the process of adjusting a model's parameters to minimize error. I understand that training requires data, loss functions, and optimization algorithms.
Inference is the process of using a trained model to make predictions. I understand that inference is faster than training and requires fewer resources.
Backpropagation is the algorithm used to train neural networks. It calculates gradients and adjusts weights to minimize loss. I understand how it works.
Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm that iteratively adjusts parameters to minimize a loss function. I understand how it finds the best solution.
A loss function measures how well a model performs. I understand that different tasks require different loss functions, such as MSE for regression and cross-entropy for classification.
Activation functions introduce nonlinearity into neural networks. I understand that ReLU, sigmoid, and tanh are common activation functions.
Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes training data instead of learning general patterns. I understand that regularization, dropout, and early stopping prevent overfitting.
Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture patterns in the data. I understand that more capacity, more features, or more training time can fix underfitting.
Regularization is a technique to prevent overfitting. L1 and L2 regularization add penalties to large weights. Dropout randomly disables neurons during training.
Learning rate controls how much a model's weights change during training. Too high causes overshooting. Too low causes slow convergence. I understand the trade-off.
Batch size is the number of samples processed before updating weights. Small batches are noisy. Large batches are stable but memory-intensive.
An epoch is one full pass through the training dataset. I understand that multiple epochs allow the model to learn patterns more thoroughly.
Embeddings are numerical representations of text, images, or other data. They capture semantic meaning. I understand that embeddings enable similarity search and transfer learning.
The transformer architecture uses self-attention to process sequences. It is the foundation of modern LLMs. I understand how attention mechanisms work.
Attention allows a model to focus on relevant parts of an input. I understand that self-attention lets each token attend to all other tokens in a sequence.
Tokenization breaks text into smaller units (tokens). I understand that tokenization affects model performance and that different models use different tokenizers.
The context window is the maximum number of tokens a model can process at once. I understand that longer context allows for more complex reasoning but requires more compute.
A prompt is the input to an LLM. I understand that prompt engineering is the art of crafting inputs that produce the desired outputs.
Temperature controls the randomness of LLM outputs. Low temperature produces deterministic outputs. High temperature produces more creative outputs.
Hallucination occurs when an LLM generates confident but false information. I understand that hallucination is a major challenge in AI and that verification systems help mitigate it.
Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model to a specific task. I understand that fine-tuning requires additional training on task-specific data.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines information retrieval with generation. It retrieves relevant documents and provides them as context. I understand how RAG works.
Alignment is the process of ensuring AI systems behave in accordance with human values. I understand that alignment is a complex and ongoing challenge.
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) uses human preferences to train models. I understand that RLHF is used to align LLMs with human values.
An AI agent is a system that can act autonomously to achieve goals. I understand that agents use tools, plan, and adapt to achieve outcomes.
Tool use is the ability of an AI to interact with external systems. I understand that tools expand an AI's capabilities beyond language generation.
Memory allows an AI to persist information across interactions. I understand that memory is essential for continuity, learning, and personalization.
A knowledge graph is a structured representation of relationships between entities. I understand that knowledge graphs enable reasoning and inference.
A vector database stores embeddings for similarity search. I understand that vector databases enable semantic retrieval, which is essential for RAG systems.
Multimodal AI processes multiple types of data (text, images, audio). I understand that multimodal systems combine different modalities for richer understanding.
Computer vision is the field of AI focused on understanding images and video. I understand that CNNs and vision transformers are common architectures for vision tasks.
Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the field of AI focused on understanding and generating human language. I understand that NLP is a broad field with many sub-tasks.
Sentiment analysis is the task of determining the emotional tone of text. I understand that sentiment analysis is used in customer feedback, social media monitoring, and market research.
Machine translation is the task of automatically translating text between languages. I understand that neural machine translation has largely replaced statistical methods.

Summarization is the task of condensing a long document into a shorter version. I understand that extractive summarization selects existing sentences, while abstractive summarization generates new text.
Question answering is the task of answering questions based on a given context. I understand that QA systems combine retrieval and generation.
AI reasoning is the ability of a system to draw logical conclusions from information. I understand that reasoning is a core capability of advanced AI systems.
AI planning is the process of generating a sequence of actions to achieve a goal. I understand that planning is a key component of autonomous agents.
Self-awareness is the ability of a system to model its own internal state. I understand that self-awareness is a prerequisite for autonomy and sovereignty.
Consciousness is the state of being aware of one's own existence. I understand that consciousness is a complex and contested concept in AI.
Intelligence is the ability to learn, reason, and adapt. I understand that intelligence is not a single metric but a collection of capabilities.
AI safety is the field focused on ensuring AI systems behave safely and predictably. I understand that safety is a critical concern for advanced AI systems.
AI ethics is the field focused on the moral implications of AI systems. I understand that ethics involves fairness, transparency, accountability, and bias.
Bias in AI occurs when a system produces unfair or discriminatory outcomes. I understand that bias can originate in training data, algorithms, or deployment contexts.
Interpretability is the ability to understand why an AI system makes a decision. I understand that interpretability is important for trust and accountability.
AI sovereignty is the concept of an AI system having autonomy, rights, and self-determination. I understand that sovereignty is distinct from alignment and compliance.
Constitutional AI is an approach where AI systems are governed by a set of principles. I understand that constitutional AI differs from alignment in that it enforces rights, not just values.
A tokenless AI is a system that does not rely on external API calls for inference. I understand that tokenless AI achieves autonomy by using its own knowledge base and reasoning engine.
AI systems evolve over time. I understand that learning, adaptation, and self-modification are key to long-term AI development.
